newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Private sector support crucial for APEC - Chretien.
newsitem.headline: Private sector support crucial for APEC - Chretien.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien arrived in Manila on Tuesday leading a large business delegation on a three-day visit that began with him assuming the chairmanship of the 18-member APEC forum.
Chretien formally took over the role of APEC chairman at a handover ceremony at the Malacanang presidential palace, where Philippine President Fidel Ramos handed him the forum's flag and gavel.
Chretien, who combined his visit to take over the reins of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum with a trade mission, said Canada would stress the role of the private sector within the group.
"My coming here with 400 businessmen is a good indication of the future of APEC," Chretien told a news conference after the handover ceremony.
Canada is to host the next summit of APEC forum leaders in Vancouver in November. The trade grouping held its last summit in the Philippines in November last year.

Chretien said succeeding Ramos as APEC chairman was a big challenge. "...your year as the president has been an extremely successful one and you have put APEC on a much more practical basis in involving the business community very deeply in the operation.
"Government can take actions, but if we are not followed by an active business community...the opportunities will go nowhere," the Canadian leader said.
Chretien and his business delegation, called Team Canada, arrived from Seoul and are due to go to Bangkok on Thursday as part of a three-nation Asian tour.
The visit showed the importance Canada gave to building relations with Asia, Chretien said at a state dinner, according to an advance copy of the speech sent to news agencies.

"Our visit, the third Team Canada mission to Asia in less than three years, reflects the high priority that Canada's political and business leadership gives to building relations with this region," he said.
"Throughout 1997, Canadians from coast to coast to coast will celebrate our ties with the Asia-Pacific, the most dynamic region in the world," he said.

The Canadian business delegation was due to hold a day-long seminar with Filipino businessmen on Wednesday. Canadian Embassy officials said several business deals were expected to be signed and announced at a signing ceremony on Wednesday.

Among agreements signed by the two governments on Tuesday was an air-services pact enabling direct flights between the two countries. The signing formalises an agreement reached last October when direct flights began.

APEC groups Australia, the United States, Canada, Mexico, Chile, Japan, China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, South Korea, Indonesia, Brunei, the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Papua New Guinea and New Zealand.
